notes: The discount propagation pipeline flows through three stages: (1) mapDispatchPriceReport in submit-reservations.mappers.ts initializes dispatch price reports with discount=undefined, (2) applyReportDiscountsService matches order-line-item discounts to dispatches via lineItem.id and writes discount into dispatch.report.price.discount, (3) mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch passes discount through to the Mozio payload. The bug is most likely in stage (2) where the lineItem.id match fails for return-trip line items (return legs may have different IDs or be nested under a modification), and in getTicketPricePerUnit which may compute the wrong discount-per-unit when isReturnTrip=true because it uses the parent orderLineItem's isReturn flag rather than the dispatch line item's modification metadata.

acceptanceCriteria: When a promo-code discount is associated with a return-trip line item, the discount must be propagated into the corresponding return-trip dispatch's report.price.discount field, regardless of whether the return-trip line item carries a different ID or is identified via modification metadata rather than a direct ID match.

When computing the discount-per-unit value for a return-trip dispatch, the system must use the return-leg discount data (not the outbound-leg discount data) so that the per-unit discount reflects the actual discount applied to the return portion of the order.

When a promo code applies only to the outbound leg, the return-trip dispatch.report.price.discount must remain undefined in the submit-order payload — no zero-value discount object must be injected by the discount-propagation logic.

When a single promo code covers a round-trip booking, both the outbound and return dispatch.report.price.discount.amount values must reflect their independently applied discount amounts (not the same total duplicated on both dispatches).
No regression: outbound-trip promo code discount display remains unchanged for orders that do not include a return trip.

The discount field from dispatch.report.price.discount must be preserved through the sanitization/mapping pipeline for return-trip dispatches without being dropped or overwritten at any stage between initial price-report construction and final Mozio payload emission.

The system must correctly handle promo-code discount propagation for return-trip dispatches in three distinct scenarios: (a) promo applies only to the return leg — return dispatch carries the discount, outbound does not; (b) promo applies to both legs — each dispatch carries its independently computed discount amount; (c) promo applies only to the outbound leg — return dispatch carries no discount object in the payload.
When a return-trip dispatch has a return-leg discount, the computed discount-per-unit value must reflect the return-leg discount amount, not the outbound-leg discount amount.
The promo code discount amount for the return trip must be rendered in the Mozio email confirmation using the same locale and currency format conventions as the outbound trip discount display.
The promo code discount amount for the return trip must be included in the Mozio email confirmation HTML template for all supported locales, not just the default locale.

When a promo code does not apply to the return portion of a round-trip booking, the Mozio email confirmation must display a discount amount of zero for the return trip rather than omitting the discount field entirely.

When only one trip segment of a round-trip booking is discounted, the system must not duplicate or misapply that segment's discount amount to the other segment's line item in either the submit-order payload or the email confirmation.

When multiple promo codes are applied to a single round-trip order, each dispatch's report.price.discount.amount must reflect the sum of all promo-code discounts applicable to that specific leg, without cross-leakage between outbound and return.

When a return-trip line item has no associated discount (e.g., the promo code is outbound-only and the return leg has no separate promo), the discount-propagation pipeline must not throw, log an error, or produce a malformed price-report object for the return dispatch.
